set.srv.socks.hint: send this server's traffic through a SOCKS5 proxy, as host:port. The proxy looks up the server's name for you, so the lookup does not leak past it. Blank connects directly. Each server has its own, so one provider can go through a proxy while the others do not
set.srv.socksauth.hint: only if your proxy asks for a user name and password. Leave both blank for an open proxy. Like the server password above, a stored proxy password is never shown: leave it blank to keep it, or clear the user name to remove both
set.srv.test.capacity: your plan will not give this many connections at once. Lower the connection count.
set.srv.test.permanent: the server rejected the sign-in. Check the username and password.
set.srv.test.title: Connect and authenticate to check this server is reachable
set.srv.testall.title: Connect and authenticate to every server at once
set.srv.title: Usenet servers
set.srv.tls.title: Encrypted connection to this server
set.srv.tuned.old: last measured {n} connections {d}d ago, too old to apply
set.srv.tuned.title: auto-connections measured this provider is fastest at {n} sockets: more were slower. Turn off auto-connections (Connection tuning) to use your set value.
set.srv.warm.hint: reuse this server's connections between downloads instead of opening new ones, so the next one starts sooner. Whether it helps depends on your link, so it is off until you measure it: Measure runs a short paired test and tells you what it found
set.ui.addask.hint: adding an .nzb from this page opens a small panel first: which category it belongs to (that is the folder it ends up in), what priority, and the archive password if you already know it needs one. Off adds straight away with the usual settings, the way it always did. Downloads sent by Sonarr, Radarr, an RSS feed or the watch folder are never asked about. Stored in this browser
set.ui.cards.hint: which cards the dashboard shows, how tightly each one is packed, and the order they run in. Works the same by touch, mouse or keyboard, and is stored in this browser. On a desktop the same three things are on each card itself: drag its handle to move it, and the two buttons beside the handle compact or hide it
set.ui.compact.hint: tighten every dashboard card so all the figures fit in a small window: same numbers, less padding. Individual cards can be compacted on their own with the density button in the card header; stored in this browser
set.ui.customcss.hint: create this file and it loads after the built-in styles, so your rules win without needing !important. Reload a page to see a change; an upgrade replaces the dashboard but never your file.
set.ui.drop.hint: where the two targets sit when you drag a file onto the page, and which of them gets the room. Stored in this browser
set.ui.herohist.hint: the bar chart under the throughput graph, showing how much time you spend at each speed. Useful for spotting a line that never reaches its peak, noise if you just want the live rate. Stored in this browser
set.ui.histcolor.hint: green for completed, red for failed. Off leaves the names plain - the coloured dot and the row's details still say which is which
set.ui.histrows.hint: how many finished downloads the History card lists before you expand it with the ▤ button; drag the card's bottom edge to make the list scroll instead. Applies to every device viewing this daemon.
set.ui.install.hint: gives nzbfast its own window and its own icon in your dock or taskbar, with no tab strip or address bar around it. It is still this daemon on this machine: nothing is uploaded, and nothing extra is downloaded. The window is tied to the address you are on, so if you ever change the daemon's port, install it again from the new one.
set.ui.install.ios: Tap the Share button, then "Add to Home Screen".
set.ui.install.safari: In Safari, choose File, then "Add to Dock".
set.ui.lang.hint: how this browser shows nzbfast: "System" follows your device language; stored in this browser
set.ui.langd.hint: for embedded webviews and browsers that haven't chosen: "Auto" follows each device's language
set.ui.layout.hint: the mode that labels every card's move, resize, compact and hide controls, and the button that forgets this browser's hidden cards, card order and chart sizes
set.ui.mediachipcolor.hint: tints the resolution/codec chip: violet for AV1, HEVC and VP9, blue for H.264, nothing for the older formats. Off leaves it plain - the chip still spells the codec out either way, and a chip whose bytes do not match its name stays amber
set.ui.notify.hint: a system notification when a download completes or fails; the browser will ask permission
set.ui.preview: Check a file while it downloads
set.ui.preview.hint: each download's details can be read out of the video file itself while it arrives: resolution, codecs, audio languages, subtitles, chapters. It is how you catch a release that is the wrong cut, the wrong language or upscaled, before the rest of it downloads. "Details and a player" also offers the file in this page for the formats your browser opens; anything it cannot open still opens in your own player, and nothing is ever converted. Off stops the file being read at all.
set.ui.provsort.hint: seconds between re-ordering the Providers list by live speed (rows slide to their new spot); default 10, 0 keeps the configured order; stored in this browser
set.ui.shapechipcolor.hint: tints the chip describing what unpacking took: violet for encrypted, blue when there was no compression to undo or nothing had to land on disk first. Off leaves it plain - the chip still says the same thing in words
set.ui.title: Interface
set.ui.units.hint: how every speed is shown: megabytes (MB/s, the download-manager norm) or megabits (Mb/s, how ISPs quote line speeds). File sizes stay in bytes either way. Applies to every device viewing this daemon.
set.watchdir.autoretry: Try a failed download again after
set.watchdir.autoretry.hint: a download that failed because articles were missing is queued again once, this long afterwards: a post can still be arriving at your provider, and waiting is the only thing that fixes that. Minutes; 0 = never retry on its own. Default 20. A failure that was the connection rather than the post waits 2 minutes instead, and a job that has already had its one automatic try is left in History for you to decide about
set.watchdir.cleanup.hint: file extensions or name patterns deleted from a job's folder once it completes successfully, e.g. sfv, srr, url, *sample*, Subs/*; empty = off. Recovery files have their own switch above
set.watchdir.cleanupmode.hint: what happens to the leftovers cleanup removes once a download finishes: spent archive parts, recovery files, samples and other junk. Following the setting above keeps one rule for everything; always Trash keeps leftovers recoverable even when your own deletes are permanent; always permanent removes them outright, which keeps a busy Trash from filling up with archive parts. Files you delete yourself always follow the setting above
set.watchdir.cleanupmode.trash: always go to the Trash or Recycle Bin
set.watchdir.dir.hint: .nzb files dropped here are queued as soon as they land; empty = off
set.watchdir.eatvols: When the unpack will not fit
set.watchdir.eatvols.always: always delete each part as it is used up
set.watchdir.eatvols.hint: some archives cannot be unpacked as they arrive: every part is written to disk first and opened afterwards, so the disk holds the parts and the unpacked files at the same time. A password-protected set needs a third copy, because unlocking writes the plain copy beside the encrypted one before swapping them. That is why a download can fail at 96% on a disk that had room for it. With this on, each archive part is deleted outright the moment the unpacker has read the last of it, so the peak is about one part plus the largest file inside. Deleted for real, not moved to the Trash: the point is space back this second. Only ever on a download that has verified. If it stops halfway, the download is fetched again, which is exactly what already happens when the disk fills, so this can only make the good case cheaper
set.watchdir.eatvols.lowdisk: when the disk is too full, ask me per download
set.watchdir.eatvols.off: keep every part until the unpack finishes
set.watchdir.extunrar.hint: use the unrar program installed on this machine instead of nzbfast's built-in extractor. An escape hatch for archives that fail to unpack: the built-in path is faster on every shape we have benchmarked, so leave this off unless one does. Hash-named obfuscated posts always use the built-in path, whose renaming unrar cannot follow. Needs unrar next to the nzbfast binary or on the system PATH
set.watchdir.extunrar.missing: unrar is not installed, so nzbfast keeps unpacking with its built-in extractor. Install unrar, or put it beside the nzbfast program, and this setting takes effect on the very next unpack.
set.watchdir.faillink.hint: some indexers attach a report link to every NZB they serve. Telling them a post is dead is how they learn to stop offering it, and they usually answer with another copy of the same title. Only works for NZBs fetched by URL (RSS, Add-by-URL, your indexer's "send to" button) - a file you dropped in yourself carries no link. Off by default: it tells a third party what failed for you
set.watchdir.faillink.regrab: report it and queue another copy
set.watchdir.finish.hint: what to do once every download is finished, including its repair and unpack. Sleep and shut down warn first, with a countdown across the top of this page and a button to stop it, and switch themselves back to "nothing" once they have run, so a machine that wakes up does not go straight back to sleep. Neither fires while a paused download is still in the queue. Running a script is left on and runs every time. Most installs have no permission to sleep or shut down the machine; if it fails, nzbfast says so in the log and leaves everything running
set.watchdir.finishdelay: Warn before sleeping or shutting down for
set.watchdir.finishdelay.hint: how long the countdown across the top of the page runs before the machine sleeps or shuts down, so you have time to stop it. Seconds, 0 to 3600; default 60. Set 0 if nobody is at the screen anyway
set.watchdir.finishscript.hint: run when the queue empties, if the choice above is "run a script". It gets no download to work on - there is no single job - so it is handed NZBFAST_EVENT=queue_finished and nothing else. The post-processing script above is the one that runs per download. It shares the time limit set for that script
set.watchdir.interval.hint: a file dropped on this machine is noticed the moment it lands, so this is only the backstop for folders the system cannot report on: typically a network share written from another computer. Seconds, 1 to 3600; default 5
set.watchdir.keep.hint: leave the original .nzb in the watch folder after it is queued, instead of moving it to the Trash. For collectors, and for handing the file to someone when a download misbehaves. A kept file is remembered and not queued again; re-save it to download it again. Whatever you choose, every job's drawer can save you a copy of its .nzb
set.watchdir.openscript.title: Open the folder containing this script
set.watchdir.outage: Give up on a server that is not answering after
set.watchdir.outage.hint: when a server stops accepting connections - it is unreachable, or your account is at its connection limit - anything only that server has is stuck until it comes back. This is how long a download waits, counting up all the time that server has been out, before carrying on without it. The download then ends as a connection failure, which is retried on its own a couple of minutes later and picks up where it left off, so nothing is lost. Minutes; default 15. Set 0 to wait however long it takes instead: the download will sit there rather than ever come back failed, which is what you want for something you may not find again - other downloads still go ahead of it. Either way its row names the server and how long it has been out
set.watchdir.parclean.hint: a download's .par2 repair files have done their job once everything verifies, so they are removed when it completes successfully. Turn off to keep them in the download folder
set.watchdir.prequeue.hint: runs before every add with SABnzbd's pre-queue args + SAB_* env vars, and can rename, recategorize, reprioritize or reject the download before it queues; a rejected add goes to history with the reason. Empty = off. A script that fails or answers nonsense never blocks the add
set.watchdir.prequeuetimeout: Give the pre-queue script at most
set.watchdir.prequeuetimeout.hint: an add waits on this script, so its budget is short. A script still over it is killed and the add proceeds untouched. Seconds; 0 = no limit; default 30
set.watchdir.pwfile.hint: a plain text file, one password per line, tried top to bottom whenever a download is password-protected and no working password came with it - the same file format SABnzbd and NZBGet use, so you can point all three at one file. Edit it in any text editor; changes count from the very next attempt. A password that works is kept on that download
set.watchdir.pwprompt: When an archive needs a password
set.watchdir.pwprompt.hint: "ask right away" prompts the moment a running download turns out to be password-protected, so you can type it while it keeps downloading; "ask when finished" waits until the download completes and offers the 🔑 unlock; "never ask" completes the download quietly with the archive left packed in its folder for you to extract by hand. Set password on the download itself works in every mode
set.watchdir.recursive.hint: files in subfolders are picked up too, and the first subfolder's name becomes the download's category: a file dropped in watch/tv joins the tv category. A folder named "rejected" is left alone; it is where unusable files go when the switch below is on
set.watchdir.refeed: Queue NZB files a download produces
set.watchdir.refeed.hint: some posts are a "container": a small NZB whose payload is another .nzb file. With this on, a download that finishes with an NZB among its files adds that NZB to the queue paused, so you can check its size and start it yourself. It goes one level only, an NZB inside a download that itself arrived this way is left alone; candidate files over 32 MB are skipped, at most 20 per download are taken, and anything that is not a readable NZB is left on disk
set.watchdir.rejected.hint: a file that is not a usable NZB is moved into a "rejected" folder inside the watch folder, with a small text file beside it saying what was wrong. Off: the file stays where you put it and the reason is shown above the queue. A file that merely looks incomplete is always left in place, because it may still be arriving
set.watchdir.sandbox.hint: the external unrar and par2 helpers, and your own scripts, are run inside a confinement box where this machine offers one. Nothing to set here: this reports what is in force. Where none is available the helpers run exactly as they always have, so a download never fails for want of it
set.watchdir.script.hint: runs after every job. Both contracts are spoken, so a script written for either downloader works unchanged: SABnzbd's 8 arguments and SAB_* variables, and NZBGet's NZBPP_ / NZBOP_ / NZBPR_ variables with the 93/94/95 exit codes. Name several, separated by commas, to run them in that order - each one sees what the one before it did, and a failure part-way through does not cancel the rest. Empty = off
set.watchdir.scriptconfine.hint: runs your scripts so they can only write inside the folders nzbfast already uses: the download folder, any move-to destinations, the watch folder and the system temporary folder. They keep full read access and full network access, so notifiers and library tools work as before. Turn this off if a script needs to write somewhere else and fails with "operation not permitted". This does nothing on a machine with no confinement available - the line below says which yours has
set.watchdir.scripttimeout.hint: a script still running after this is killed, and a line saying so goes in the log; the download itself is unaffected either way. Seconds; 0 = wait as long as it takes, which is what a long transcode wants. Default 3600. With no limit, one script that hangs holds a thread for as long as nzbfast runs, and every job that finishes after it holds another

set.watchdir.trash: Deleted files go to the Trash
set.watchdir.trash.hint: cleanup moves files to the system Trash or Recycle Bin instead of deleting them, so a wrong guess about what was junk can be undone. If the Trash ever refuses a file, it is left where it is rather than deleted outright. On by default on macOS and Windows. Off on Linux, where there is usually no desktop Trash to empty: with it on, files go to a hidden .Trash folder on the same disk as your downloads, and that space stays used until you empty it yourself
